direct_claims: This chart tracks how many countries worldwide had different types of COVID-19-related restrictions on international travel arrivals over time.
The time span shown runs from January 2020 to December 2022.
The categories shown are complete ban, partial ban, quarantine on some arrivals, screening arrivals, and no restrictions.
The source is Our World in Data using Blavatnik School of Government, University of Oxford data.

The note indicates that when policies differed within a country, the most stringent policy was used, which means the chart reflects the strictest national condition rather than an average experience across regions.
The chart does not by itself show whether these restrictions were effective at reducing infections, only how common each policy type was across countries.
Because the unit is number of countries rather than share of world population or travel volume, a policy in a small country and a large country count equally here.

Through 2021 and into 2022, the dominant categories shift away from bans and toward screening and eventually no restrictions. — derived from comparison of category shares over time

The chart indicates that by 2022 many countries had removed outright restrictions, which would have supported the recovery of cross-border movement and travel-dependent sectors. — derived in part from increase in no restrictions by 2022

The earlier prevalence of bans and partial bans likely disrupted tourism, business travel, family reunification, and some forms of labor mobility on a global scale. — derived in part from widespread restrictive categories in 2020–2021
As a result, the chart is more useful for understanding policy spread across governments than for estimating how many people or trips were affected. — derived from country-count unit
